subject: Re: Post-call recap + model fit (EU/APAC multilingual checks)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Larsen <emma.larsen@acme-europe.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap + next steps (multilingual / EU & APAC)

Emma — great to meet today. Quick recap from our discovery and proposed next steps.

What we heard:
- You need production-quality LLM features for customer support and knowledge search across EU languages (EN, FR, DE, ES) and APAC locales (JA, KO, HI).
- Key constraints: data residency for EU traffic, sub-200ms median token latency for support replies, and tight quality SLAs on locale-specific intents (refunds, legal requests).
- Current goals: pilot on 3 support flows, evaluate quality/regression by locale, then expand to 10k monthly active users.

Recommended next steps:
1) We’ll share a focused prompt set and our multilingual benchmark report (attached).
2) Redwood will propose two model configurations for evaluation (one higher-quality, one cost-optimized).
3) Run a 3-week PoC: locale-specific evals + live shadow traffic for a subset of requests.
4) Align on data residency (Dedicated/Private options) and a pricing estimate.

Attachments included: prompt_sets_acme_v1.json, multilingual_benchmarks_q1_2026.pdf.
Related links: HubSpot deal (ACME-4572), Drive folder with full benchmarks.

Open questions for you (to prep the PoC):
- Which three support flows should be prioritized? (suggestion: refunds, order status, legal requests)
- Do you have locale-specific test sets or should we run our in-house eval sets and share results?

I’ll follow up with model recommendations and an eval plan later today.

Thanks — Marissa

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Larsen <emma.larsen@acme-europe.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Rajesh Kumar <raj.kumar@asia-payments.co>
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 11:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps (multilingual / EU & APAC)

Emma — great, thanks for confirming the pilot flows and the availability of EU test sets. Below are the model recommendations and the proposed evaluation approach.

Model recommendations (for eval):
- EU high-quality: redwood-open-rlhf-large-v2 (best-in-class quality for French/German/Spanish; higher latency/cost but best for intent-sensitive flows).
- EU cost-balanced: redwood-open-medium-2.1 (good quality, lower token cost).
- APAC compact (latency/cost-optimized): redwood-multi-compact-1.0 (quantized; tuned for JA/KO/HI with good throughput).

Benchmarks & prompt sets:
- Multilingual benchmark report (link in Drive attached) — includes per-language accuracy, intent-precision, and hallucination rates.
- Prompt set: prompt_sets_acme_v1.json (attached) — contains canonical prompts for refunds, order status, cancellations per locale and annotated evaluation rubrics.

Quality/regression concerns and plan:
- Regression risk primarily when moving to quantized/compact runtimes (some drop in intent precision for low-resource languages).
- Proposed mitigation: before any rollout, run a regression suite that checks intent-precision and hallucination rate per locale (thresholds we’ll suggest in the eval plan).
- Continuous monitoring: Redwood Console will emit per-route language breakdowns and alerts for regressions versus the baseline prompt set.

Proposed PoC evaluation timeline (3 weeks):
Week 0: onboarding + data access + test set exchange
Week 1: baseline runs (EU high-quality + APAC compact) on 500 sample queries per locale
Week 2: shadowed live traffic and focused error analysis (top-50 failure cases per locale)
Week 3: final tuning, regression checks, and go/no-go decision.

Attachments: eval_plan_acme_v1.docx included.

Next steps from Redwood:
- I’ll coordinate a short kickoff with our solutions engineer (Vivek) to align on data access and residency controls.
- Vivek / Ben — can you review the attached eval plan and confirm we can commit a small Dedicated pool in EU for the pilot? (I expect a 2-GPU reserved pool will suffice for the 3-week PoC; cost/commitment TBD).

Emma — we’ll get you a formal PoC proposal and a SOW template by end of day Wednesday.

Thanks,
Marissa
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: ACME pilot ask — review eval plan & EU residency

Vivek / Ben — looping you to review the ask from Acme (ACME-DEAL-4572). Quick bullets:
- They have EU test sets for FR/DE/ES; need Redwood to provide JA/KO/HI eval sets and run baseline.
- Pilot: 3 weeks, 2-GPU EU Dedicated pool (dedicated for EU traffic due to residency).
- Objective: prove no locale-specific regression > 5% intent-precision drop vs baseline for each language.

Please review eval_plan_acme_v1.docx and advise on:
1) Reserving 2x A100-equivalent in eu-west-1 for pilot (or recommend alternate SKUs).
2) Any potential blockers for data residency/compliance we should flag (I think SOC2 + EU data processing addendum covers it but confirm).
3) Pricing — back-of-envelope for 3-week pilot (include reserved node cost + engineering support).

I’ll compile your notes into the SOW draft.

Thanks — Marissa
From: Emma Larsen <emma.larsen@acme-europe.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rajesh Kumar <raj.kumar@asia-payments.co>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 15:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + model fit (EU/APAC multilingual checks)

Thanks, team — that timeline and approach look good. We’d like to kick off the pilot the week of Mar 9 if you can get the SOW and EU Dedicated estimate over by Friday.

Questions for Redwood before we sign off on the SOW:
- Can you confirm encryption-at-rest and KMS controls for EU Dedicated?
- For APAC traffic (shadowed), we’re OK with Redwood multi-region routing as long as any persistent logs containing PII are stored in-region or anonymized.

Happy to have Rajesh manage APAC coordination — Rajesh, can you confirm the JA/KO/HI test expectations on your side?

Best — Emma
